clue.text: Getting hot about cold support

indicators.note: about means going round, so the hot word is wrapped round the cold letter

parts.note: getting hot is baking, as in an oven or the sun
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Warming up around a source of chilly encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing is help or endorsement given to someone, a synonym of support.

clue.text: Handsome, woman holding a gun finds game

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the woman's word goes round the others

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: An attractive armed woman discovers some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like quarry for the gun but is a table game played with balls and cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a board game in which balls are struck into numbered holes.

clue.text: Company of traders have, a centre for vehicles

indicators.note: have means hold, so the two vehicles contain the letter
centre means the letter sits in the middle of the vehicles

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a van is another vehicle

explanation.surface: A trading company has a depot for its lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'vehicles', supplies two pieces; 'Company' looks like a business, but here it means a travelling band.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a group of merchants travelling together, as across a desert.

clue.text: Rising man batting second wants speedy action

parts.note: in cricket, a side batting is in
urgent describes something requiring prompt action

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming cricketer batting at number two wants to score quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' means rising in revolt, not getting up or advancing in a career.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel, someone who rises up against authority.

clue.text: Lame but plucky

definitions.meaning: a ... leg is a lame one

explanation.definitionFit: Game means both crippled, of a limb, and courageous, ready for anything.

clue.text: Examine girl's school

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, here with the possessive S
a school of thought is a sect

explanation.surface: An inspector looks over a young woman's school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' here is a school of thought, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect something is to analyse it minutely, a figurative sense of examine.

clue.text: Made out nothing in the document

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the nothing word goes inside the document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a cipher is a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone found nothing written in a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made out' looks like a past tense of writing a cheque, but means read or understood.
explanation.definitionFit: To decipher is to work out the meaning of something, so made out is a synonym.

clue.text: Avail against dry and withered environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the dry word goes round the letter

parts.note: sere means dried up and withered
V is the abbreviation of versus, against

explanation.surface: Benefit is being fought against in a parched setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve can mean to be useful or suffice, as in 'that will serve', which is what avail means.

clue.text: Empty-headed, merry-making occurring in summer

indicators.note: being without a head here means losing the first letter of the word

parts.note: a festival is a time of merry-making

explanation.surface: Silly revelry on a summer's day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty-headed' looks like silly but says remove the first letter, F.
explanation.definitionFit: Estival, a variant of aestival, means belonging to the summer season.

clue.text: Going back and forth in pointless detail, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible rearrangement of what is left
pointless means without a compass point, so the letter for east is taken away

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over trivial specifics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes E (east, a compass point) from DETAIL, and 'perhaps' rearranges DTAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal describes the ebb and flow of the sea, which moves in and out.

clue.text: Chatters about the right dresses

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the chatting word goes round the right letter

parts.note: chatters means gabs, talks idly
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Gossips discuss the correct way to clothe oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dresses' is a verb: garbs clothes someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To garb is to clothe someone, so garbs is a verb synonym of dresses.

clue.text: Spice, reckoned to be softened by soaking

parts.note: mace is a spice made from the nutmeg husk
reckoned means rated, estimated

explanation.surface: A spice is judged to have gone soft after being steeped.
explanation.definitionFit: Macerated food has been steeped in liquid until it breaks down and turns tender.

clue.text: Mermaid — Keats's pet — had a great day in the lake

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the day letters go inside the lake word

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
VE Day, Victory in Europe Day in 1945, was a great day

explanation.surface: A mermaid, the poet's darling, enjoyed herself in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mermaid was an Elizabethan London inn that Keats celebrated in 'Lines on the Mermaid Tavern'; 'Mermaid' looks like a sea creature. VE Day is the 1945 Victory in Europe celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mermaid was a famous London inn, a public house Keats praised in verse.

clue.text: Violent social change caused by.. earthquake?

definitions.meaning: a revolution or sudden disruption of society
geologically, an upward lifting of the earth's crust, as a quake can cause

explanation.surface: Turmoil in society is blamed on a tremor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a sudden social disruption and the literal heaving up of the ground in a quake.

clue.text: Refuse to move, up away from the centre that is for jewellery

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a horse that jibs refuses to move on
outer means further from the middle
ie abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A stubborn person refuses to leave the centre for some trinkets.
explanation.definitionFit: Bijouterie is a collective term for jewels and trinkets, from French bijou.

clue.text: Thrust north in sledge

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the north letter goes inside the sledge

parts.note: a luge is a racing sledge

explanation.surface: Pushing a sledge forward through the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust, as in fencing.

clue.text: Drawn up like troops in parallel .. groups, to echo Lenin's original order

definitions.text: Drawn up like troops in parallel .. groups

indicators.note: an original order is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive S adds no letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers drawn up in ranks to mirror the Soviet leader's first command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original order' reads as Lenin's first command but signals that ECHO and LENIN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a stepped formation of troops or aircraft, each line parallel to the next.

clue.text: Author of "A Murderer in the Orchestra"

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the murderer goes inside the orchestra

parts.note: the Hallé is a famous Manchester orchestra
Cain killed his brother Abel, the first murderer in Genesis

explanation.surface: Who wrote the thriller with a killer among the musicians?
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title looks like a real book, but it is wordplay. The Hallé is Manchester's orchestra; Hall Caine was a popular Victorian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Hall Caine was a Manx-born novelist, a best-selling writer of the 1890s.

clue.text: Confident it's flabby

explanation.definitionFit: Without nerves, a person is unflustered; without sinews or force, a thing is limp and weak.

clue.text: Crew an unknown quantity in a .. dance

parts.note: a rowing crew is an eight
some means an unspecified amount

explanation.surface: A rowing team is somehow part of a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: An eightsome is a Scottish reel for eight dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome reel is a lively Scottish country dance for eight people.

clue.text: Greed an awful, even fatal thing if it hits you

definitions.text: even fatal thing if it hits you

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess

explanation.surface: A warning that avarice is a terrible, even deadly, affliction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' seems to describe greed but signals that GREED AN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, which can kill whoever it strikes.

clue.text: Splendid, knocking back this drink

indicators.note: knocking back means sending back, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: regal means magnificent, splendid

explanation.surface: Someone praises a beer while downing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' reads as drinking, which suits the surface, but signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a common drink.

clue.text: Birds without number from an Italian city

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the birds go round the number

parts.note: geese are birds

explanation.surface: Countless birds arrive from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like minus but means outside, its old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoese means coming from Genoa, the port city in north-west Italy.

clue.text: Curse old city scold

parts.note: ex means former, old
EC is the postcode area of the City of London
to rate is an old word for to scold

explanation.surface: Swearing at a former town for nagging.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postal district covering the City, its financial centre; RATE as scold is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or damn, a formal synonym of curse.

clue.text: One taken in by other woman

indicators.note: taken in means contained, so the one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: else means other, as in someone else
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One person was deceived by another lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being fooled but means put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a woman's first name.

clue.text: He's not on strike! He's coming early

parts.note: a rat is a strikebreaker, someone who keeps working
he is taken as the pronoun itself; the 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A worker who crosses the picket line turns up first thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Rathe is an old poetic word for early, as in Milton's 'rathe primrose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an archaic adjective meaning coming early or soon.

clue.text: Drinking challenge to wit in the — past

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely or to wit
once means formerly, in the past

explanation.surface: In days gone by, a battle of wits was fought over drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford, a sconce was a forfeit in which a diner had to down a tankard of ale in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: A sconce was an Oxford college penalty requiring the culprit to drain a large tankard, a drinking forfeit.

clue.text: Entrance a daughter by personal magnetism

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, personal magnetism

explanation.surface: Charming a girl through sheer charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a verb, to charm, but is the noun: a mine passage.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage into a mine, its way in.

clue.text: Broken reed — that's possible.

indicators.note: a possible arrangement of the letters is asked for, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving letters T H A T S

explanation.surface: A snapped reed — that could happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattered means smashed into pieces, so it is a synonym of broken.

clue.text: One Frenchman in Sam's tragedy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A man from France takes part in a tragic play by someone called Sam.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson wrote one play, the verse tragedy Irene (1749); 'Sam' is the familiar name for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene was the single stage tragedy written by Samuel Johnson.

clue.text: He interprets biblical entries in the index — eg, 'Eternity

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A scholar who explains scripture looks up eternity in an index.
explanation.definitionFit: An exegete is a commentator who expounds the meaning of scripture passages.

clue.text: See-saws with wobbles

definitions.meaning: moves up and down like a plank on a pivot

explanation.surface: A playground plank rocks unsteadily.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeter is both an American word for a see-saw ride and a verb for swaying unsteadily.
